blocks.md: Numbers in a table tell you something. A bar shooting up for a 7-day streak *shows* you something. Charts turn raw progress data — daily XP, lesson counts, streak lengths — into a picture your brain believes. That moment when a learner sees their own growth rendered visually is one of the biggest motivators in a gamified app. In this session you'll wire Recharts into your portal and make that moment real.

By the end of this session you will be able to install Recharts, build a `<BarChart>` and a `<LineChart>` from composable sub-components, add axes and a tooltip, and wrap the whole thing in `<ResponsiveContainer>` so it resizes cleanly on any screen.

**Charts make data feel real.** Streaks, daily totals, and cumulative XP are far more motivating when visualised than listed.

Recharts is a React charting library built on SVG and D3. Its big idea is **composition**: you build a chart by nesting components, not configuring a monolithic object.

```jsx
<ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height={300}>
  <BarChart data={data}>
    <XAxis dataKey="day" />
    <YAxis />
    <Tooltip />
    <Bar dataKey="xp" fill="#6366f1" />
  </BarChart>
</ResponsiveContainer>
```

`<ResponsiveContainer>` is the wrapper that reads the parent element's width at runtime and rescales the SVG — essential for dashboards that must work on both a phone and a wide monitor. Inside it you choose a chart type (`BarChart`, `LineChart`, `AreaChart`, …) and drop in the pieces you need.
Read the **Getting Started / Installation** section, install Recharts in your project, then come back.
blocks.label: Recharts — Getting Started

blocks.md: **Install once, use everywhere.** Run `npm install recharts` in your project root. Recharts ships its own TypeScript types — no `@types/recharts` needed. If you're on Vite and see a *peer dependency* warning about React 19, don't panic — it just means the library hasn't officially listed your exact React version yet. Re-run the install as `npm install recharts --legacy-peer-deps`; that flag tells npm to install anyway, and it works fine here.

questions.question: What is Recharts?
options: A React charting library that lets you compose charts from SVG-based components
A CSS utility for drawing bar charts without JavaScript
A built-in React hook for rendering data grids
A wrapper around the native HTML <canvas> element
questions.explanation: Recharts is a React-first charting library built on SVG and D3 where you compose charts from individual components.

questions.question: What is `<ResponsiveContainer>` for in Recharts?
options: It provides accessible ARIA labels for screen readers
It wraps a chart so it fills its parent's width and resizes automatically
It lazy-loads chart data from an API endpoint
It applies a responsive CSS grid to multiple charts on the page
questions.explanation: `<ResponsiveContainer>` reads the parent element's dimensions at runtime and rescales the SVG chart to fit, making it work on any screen size.

questions.question: How are Recharts charts constructed?
options: By calling a single `createChart()` function with a large config object
By writing raw SVG elements and wiring up D3 scales manually
By composing multiple React components such as `<BarChart>`, `<XAxis>`, `<Tooltip>`, and `<Bar>`
By importing a JSON chart definition and passing it to a `<Chart>` renderer
questions.explanation: Recharts uses composition — you nest specialized components inside a chart-type component, adding only the pieces (axes, tooltip, legend, data series) that you need.

blocks.md:
You now know why charts matter in a gamified learning portal and how Recharts makes them easy to build in React. The key ideas:

- Charts turn numbers into motivating visuals — streaks and totals land harder as bars or lines.
- Recharts composes a chart from small, focused components (`<BarChart>`, `<XAxis>`, `<YAxis>`, `<Tooltip>`, `<Bar>`).
- `<ResponsiveContainer>` wraps the chart so it adapts to any screen width automatically.

Next up you'll wire these charts to real user-state data.
bullets: Charts visualise streaks and totals so learners feel their progress.
Recharts is React-based, SVG-powered, and built by composition.
`<ResponsiveContainer>` makes every chart responsive with zero extra CSS.
